correctness.rationale: Ito isometry gives an exact joint objective over step weights and sensor precisions. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz eliminates precision variables. Strict monotone rearrangement and clipping reduce global minimization to positive nondecreasing step functions. An initial-zero-interval perturbation and refinement show each of n jumps is active. Midpoint jump locations, centroid equations and a strictly decreasing scalar equation yield the unique global stationary design, and all degeneracies are excluded. Exact symbolic covariance identities, n=2 rational case and 16,800 random supplementary designs passed the standalone verifier; these numerical cases are not substitutes for the global proof.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural end-to-end numerical-information allocation question—where to observe and how precisely—at every finite sensor count and budget, with a unique estimator and exact Bayes risk. The non-obvious finite-budget terminal concentration, the fixed-total-precision continuum limit with a strictly excluded initial interval, and strict improvement with sensor count are structural and not small perturbations of the prior noiseless grid. The result does not purport to optimize other kernels, nonlinear/adaptive sensing or arbitrary path-linear information.
